title: Nine Days on the Sideboard
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：banana　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 banana 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my uncle brought home ① a banana and the whole street came to look at it, and my grandmother said the looking was the expensive part. The ② banana, meaning the fruit and not the occasion, sat on the sideboard for nine days and was eaten on the tenth; a banana, she said, is the only food that is admired before it is understood.

Every ③ banana in that shop arrived on a Thursday and was gone by the Monday, and the ④ banana on the top shelf, meaning the one reserved for somebody and not either of those, went brown and was given away in March. A banana, my mother said, is nine parts timing and one part knowing who will be ill; my uncle said the timing is the whole of the trade.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ banana was the whole of a childhood, meaning the first one and not the fruit. The ⑥ banana, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only taste that arrives once and is measured against for forty years; a banana, he said, is either something you peel or the only standard you cannot reach twice. She said the standard is the cruel half.

By 1971 the ⑦ banana had become a word in an argument about money, and the argument had become a habit. The ⑧ banana of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in June, was nine years of Thursdays and one brown fruit; a banana, he said, is either the thing on the sideboard or the reason the street came in. She said the street was the part that mattered.

The ⑨ banana I remember is the one on the sideboard, which nobody was allowed to touch and everybody was allowed to see. A ⑩ banana, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only fruit that improves by being waited for; every banana, she said, is an occasion that has agreed to look like food. She said the food was the excuse.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 香蕉（指那个水果，与那件事／那个场合相对）
C. 固定搭配：bring home a banana 带一根香蕉回家
D. n. 香蕉（指店里每一根）
E. n. 香蕉（指顶层架子上那一根）
F. n. 香蕉（指整个童年，即第一次的味道）
G. n. 香蕉（抽象：记忆与标准）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a banana and the whole street came to look at it
The banana, meaning the fruit and not the occasion
the banana on the top shelf
banana was the whole of a childhood
the banana had become a word in an argument about money
The banana of the whole thing
A banana, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: bring home a banana 意为“带一根香蕉回家”，1959 年叔叔带了一根香蕉回家，整条街的人都来看。
banana 意为“香蕉”，指那个水果而不是那个场合，它在餐具柜上放了九天，第十天才被吃掉。
banana 指店里每一根香蕉，那家店里每一根都是星期四到货，星期一之前就卖完了。
banana 指顶层架子上那一根（留给某个人的那根），它放坏了，三月送了人。
banana 意为“香蕉”，指整个童年，即第一次的味道，而不是水果本身。
banana 为抽象用法，指记忆与标准，是唯一只来一次、却要被拿来比上四十年的味道。
banana 意为“香蕉”，到 1971 年这个 banana 成了一场关于钱的争吵里的一个词。
banana 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，叔叔六月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个星期四和一根烂掉的香蕉。
banana 意为“香蕉”，我记得的是餐具柜上那一根，谁也不许碰，谁都可以看。
banana 为抽象总称，祖母说香蕉是唯一会因为被人等着而变好的水果。
